Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Jan. 30, 1919. Mrs. E. J. Ferchan, Suquamish, Wash. Dear Madam: Lyle Mason has not been sick since her arrival at Cushman if we except a slight cold. We have had no influenza since November 15, 1918. I will advise Lyle of her father's anxiety, and will insist on her writing him immediately. Very truly yours, Superintendent EHH-S Squamanish, Wash. Jan 26 - 1919 Dept. of Cushman School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: I am writing to inquire about Lyla Hason. Her father has written to her, letting her know of the death of his wife and baby. All of them have been ill with influenza—at one time. He is very slowly getting well and has been looking for word from Lyla, so that he is becoming alarmed. at not receiving any letter. I trust Lyla is well, but if she is ill and not able to write—please do notify him. Very sincerely, (Mrs) E.J. Fencham Squamish - Wash. Jan 26 Dear Lyla: I'm enclosing these few lines and a dollar your father sends you in a letter to the superintendent of the school. Your father is slowly gaining strength—and the children are well. Thos Mary was a long time getting well. She is not able to walk yet, but I think she will be strong enough this week. Please write to your father; he feels so badly and needs your sympathy. Lovingly your friend, Emma J. Serchau. Receive $1,00. Lyla Mason. Enrolled Oct. 20, 1915 Returned Sept. 5, 1917 Withdrawn June 16, 1918 (term expired) 5-192 BRIEF. The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Attention is invited to Circulars Nos. 1039 and 1044, which must be observed. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." Dec. 28, 1917. The Mayor, Ketchikan, Alaska. Dear Sir: Fannie Shairi, the Indian wife of a Japanese writes to her daughter Lyla Mason that she is in a destitute condition having been deserted by her husband and she is in the last stages of consumption with no one to take care of her. I am advising you of this in order that the city authorities may take steps to aid her. Very respectfully, EHH S Superintendent Ketchikan, Alaska Dec 2nd 1917 Miss Layla Mason Cushman School My dear Daughter, Just a few lines to you this afternoon to let you know that I am very sick. I can't get out of bed at all. I have nobody to look after myself & my children. You know I have no relatives of my very own. I am just all alone in this world; the father of my children has taken two of my youngsters. But I got another smaller girl 1 year old. There is lot of times that I don't eat nothing for a whole solid day because I have no body to look after me. If nobody comes up to see me for a whole day, then I can't get nothing to eat at all, because I cannot move around myself. I can't afford to pay anybody to look after me. I had to borrow money last April to send you, but you didn't come when you got it. I took sick first of June, I never got to pay for it. I just sent some more money to you last Aug. but you didn't say nothing about it. Every time I write to you I would ask you about the money, but you would never mention it at all. I want you to come if you can. If the School could help pay your fare up here; I am sending you my ring. Keep it as long as you live. This is all for this time. Love to your Fanny Shaini RECORD OF PUPIL IN SCHOOL RECORD OF... Lyla Mason (Name.) Cushman Trades School. Tacoma, Wash. (Name of school.) (Location.)
